title: Add SHA-keyed CI result reuse with local fallback (ci-routing item 4)
summary: Per the user's reply, only item 4 of ci-routing.md section 10 is in scope. Add a CI result record keyed by commit SHA, the SHA check and missing/red/stale rules of 5.3, and a local fallback, in athena-core with tests, then mark item 4 in section 10. The audience is the owner, who judges by tests that fail without the SHA check or the fallback.

defaults_applied.how: Tests plus clippy and fmt criteria.
Criteria check stale, fallback, red and blocked behavior through tests.
A criterion requires blocked rather than verified when no result exists.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Per the user's reply, the scope is item 4 only; this overrides the earlier readings' scope.
The record is read by Athena from the platform API for the exact SHA, as in 5.2 and 6.2.
New logic is a pure, testable module in athena-core, with the runner and fetch injected so tests need no network.
The wait bound for an unfinished run is a parameter; its value comes from later measurement data.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test --locked`: new tests pass showing a CI result whose SHA differs from the candidate's is ignored (stale) and never yields a verified outcome; each test fails if the SHA comparison is removed.

Run `cargo test --locked`: tests show a missing, unfinished, cancelled, skipped or timed-out CI result selects the local fallback, which runs the three checks once and records them as local, keyed by SHA.

Run `cargo test --locked`: a red CI result for the matching SHA is a failed check and the fallback is not run to hide it; a green run with a workflow file changed in the same candidate is not trusted and falls back locally.
Run `cargo test --locked`: when neither CI nor the local run can produce a result, the outcome is blocked with a named reason, not verified (no empty success).
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
The record holds the run address, full SHA, per-step conclusions and duration, and Athena (not the verifier) is what reads it; the verifier command set in athena.toml is unchanged.
Section 10 item 4 of docs/design/ci-routing.md states what was built and what remains; items 5-7 are untouched, and no speedup is claimed.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the result-reuse change.

out_of_scope: Items 6-7: after-measurement with xtask walltime and the final docs job
Letting the verifier fetch the CI result itself
departures: Slightly higher cost than the reference: new module with injected fetch and fallback logic in a large core crate.
